title: Export Orchestrator for Regional Evidence Delivery and Archival Rotations
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a resilient export orchestration layer that produces tenant-scoped compliance evidence bundles (PDF/CSV/JSON) on a configurable schedule, supports regional residency targets, and rotates archived snapshots. Key goals: incremental (delta) exports to minimize bandwidth and processing, content-addressed chunking for resumable uploads, tenant-specific encryption keys and KMS signatures, and a delivery SLA with retry/backoff and observable delivery metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Configurable schedule per-tenant and per-region with timezone-aware cron definitions
Exports can be generated as full snapshots or incremental deltas (since last snapshot) and include a signed manifest with content hashes
Bundles support multiple formats: PDF evidence reports, CSV event exports, and JSON audit ledgers
Per-tenant encryption: exports encrypted with tenant KMS key; manifest contains key ID and signature
Delivery channels: S3 (region/replication-aware), secure SFTP, and webhook-to-cloud-storage gateways; fallback policy with retries and exponential backoff
Retention/rotation policies applied to archive storage with automated prune and legal-hold override
Audit trail and delivery status visible in Console: last-run, success/failure, bytes, duration, and signed-manifest hash
Operational runbook for failures with automated alerting to oncall and per-tenant SLA metrics
notes: We should avoid reinventing transfer protocols; prefer S3 multipart with server-side encryption where possible and use signed manifests for verification.
Incremental exports will rely on an event-sourced change log (ENG-49110) — coordination required to ensure idempotency and consistent snapshots.
For legal-hold tenants we must skip rotation deletions; mark manifests accordingly to prevent accidental prune.
Consider making manifest format v1.0 extensible: include content-addressed chunk list, compression algo, encryption metadata, and provenance fields.
We need a clear privacy-preserving redaction strategy for exported artifacts; redaction rules should be tenant-configurable and applied before snapshot generation.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Ava Chen: Drafted initial scope. Top risks: KMS integrations (cross-region keys), scale of generating PDFs for large tenants.
2026-03-03 - Marcus López: Punted attachment signing to manifest rather than embedding binary signatures to keep downloads lightweight.
2026-03-05 - Eng (SRE) - Priya Nair: Flagging need for backpressure/circuit-breaker when export generation queue grows > 200 concurrent jobs. See ENG-50203.
2026-03-08 - Legal - Sameer Patel: Confirmed legal-hold semantics; exports must carry legal-hold metadata and cannot be auto-pruned.
2026-03-10 - Design - Lina Park: Suggested a Console workflow that shows granular status per-tenant export with a downloadable signed-manifest and a one-click re-run for last successful export.
2026-03-12 - PM - Marcus López: Marking schema for manifests and a minimal CLI tool for partners to verify manifests as ACs evolve. Added security review flag.
suggested_rollout: Start with a beta cohort of 5 tenants (mix of small/large, multi-region) for end-to-end validation. Expose schedule UI in Console as "Collect Mode: Snapshot | Delta". Enable signed-manifests and S3 delivery by default; KMS binding as opt-in during beta.
rollout_steps: 1) API & manifest schema implemented; internal tests for manifest verification
2) Hook to event-sourced change log for delta computation (ENG-49110), unit + integration tests
3) S3 + multipart upload flow with region-aware bucket selection and retry logic
4) Tenant beta: 5 customers for 4 weeks, collect metrics on duration, bytes, retries
5) Implement Console views and allow on-demand re-run + manual download
6) Gradual ramp: +25 tenants per week with observability thresholds and throttling policies
7) Post-launch: add SFTP gateway and signed PDF watermarks per legal request
